Whether or not the template matched, no change in this repo could fix it, so declining was the right call.

The reviewer's 'may not be a recognized key' was a guess.

The README line 'directory, git, model, session, today, context' sat as unchanged context in a rewritten Quick start section, and the reviewer names the real default root in default-dsl-config.ts. e55d7b1 replaced it with the actual segment list.
guidance_note: When rewriting a README section, check every sentence that stays in the rewritten block against current code, not only the lines you edited.

evidence: The README said 'Node.js 18+' while the engines field in package.json is '^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0'. e55d7b1 aligned the README with the engines field.
guidance_note: When a PR rewrites install docs, compare stated version floors against package.json engines in the same pass.

evidence: createRequire(sourceDist) anchored at the staged dist finds no node_modules, so a re-run from the staged runtime reports 'node-shim' while stageFile's identity path keeps a prior native binary. The agent derived the kind from the staged file rather than adding a fresh-install mode, which is the sounder fix. However, its claim that a 2-byte sniff is 'a total classifier' led to F10.
guidance_note: When a status message reports what got installed, derive it from the installed artifact rather than from the lookup that chose the source.

evidence: A bare 'startsWith(binPath)' matches '<binPath>-backup', so a user command would be claimed as ours and overwritten without --force. 7923e32 made the staged-path forms whole-token matches and added tests. The agent cited types-are-the-program, but this is a string-boundary bug, not a type-representation one.
guidance_note: When deciding whether a stored command is 'ours' by path prefix, match on a token boundary from the start and write the superset-path test.

evidence: False-positive flag: e55d7b1 changed only README lines 33 and 121, and the 'Developing against a checkout' paragraph appears as an added line in the original PR diff. The sentence did say both commands 'stage the native binary', which only just deploy does, and ef4a6cd split them.
guidance_note: When one sentence offers alternative commands, state each command's own outcome rather than grouping them under one verb.

evidence: The review run that posted this finding itself checked out with @v6 successfully (run 30968857834, per the agent), so 'will fail at the Checkout step' contradicts its own existence. False-positive flag: ef4a6cd touched only README.md, and the checkout line is pre-existing context.

The reviewer concedes that 'with inputs are always strings regardless of YAML type', so no consumer value could differ. The agent also notes the file is a generated copy of the installer template. False-positive flag: ef4a6cd changed only README.md.

stagedEntryKind came from F5's fix (7923e32), not from the flagged ef4a6cd. It ignored readSync's return value, so a 0- or 1-byte file left zero bytes in Buffer.alloc(2), failed the '#!' check, and was reported as 'native'. The F5 reply had claimed the sniff was 'a total classifier'; 7c1b281 added the short-read throw.
guidance_note: When claiming a classifier is total, enumerate its input shapes, including short and empty reads, before writing it, and check every syscall's byte count.

evidence: False-positive flag: ef4a6cd touched only the Developing paragraph. The heading change from 'Quick start (macOS)' and the unscoped Cmd-click sentence both predate review, and e55d7b1 kept the Cmd-click clause while rewriting that line. The URL handler is macOS-only per step 2, so the sentence did over-promise to Linux users.
guidance_note: When widening a doc section's platform scope, re-read every sentence in it for platform-specific claims.

evidence: The agent ran a frozen-lockfile install under pnpm 10.34.5 using only this PR's package.json and workspace yaml, and all four platform packages installed. The reviewer's claim was explicitly unsure ('not clear from pnpm's public docs'). False-positive flag: 7c1b281 did not touch pnpm-workspace.yaml.

False-positive flag: resolveRenderEntry was exported in __test__ in the original PR (hunk @@ -407,4 +526,7), and 7c1b281 only touched stagedEntryKind and its test. The export had no direct test, and 8465718 added tests for both arms.
guidance_note: Every function added to a __test__ export gets at least one test per branch in the same commit that exports it.

evidence: This duplicates F13 on the same line, and the same 8465718 tests cover it. False-positive flag for the same reason: the export predates review.
guidance_note: Every function added to a __test__ export gets at least one test per branch in the same commit that exports it.

evidence: Unremoved mkdtempSync dirs were the file's existing pattern (tmpSettingsPath and the original stagedEntryKind and stageFile tests). 7c1b281 added one more test copying it, but the finding would exist without that commit, so caused_by is null. 8465718 routed every temp dir through a registered helper with an afterAll.
guidance_note: When adding tests that create temp dirs, register them for cleanup with a file-level afterAll instead of copying an unmanaged mkdtempSync pattern.

evidence: The agent showed 'git ls-files -s bin/cc-candybar' returning 100755, and the reviewer admitted 'the diff doesn't confirm' the mode. False-positive flag: the file is from the original PR, and 7c1b281 did not touch it.

False-positive flag: 8465718 changed only test files, and the bin/cc-candybar comment is from the original PR. The comment's 'loads as CommonJS regardless of the package type' was false; the agent confirmed on node 24 that extensionless files follow the type field, and d75b309 replaced the comment with the dual-home rationale.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that states runtime semantics ('regardless of X'), run the two-line experiment that confirms it.

narrative: This PR replaced postinstall machinery with a committed node bin and install-time staging. Most findings were pre-existing doc staleness or reviewer guesses that the agent correctly refuted with concrete evidence (checkout@v6, allowBuilds, supportedArchitectures, exec bit). Every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag except F10's cause is a false positive: the flagged commits were README or test-only, and the findings were on original-PR lines. The one real fix-caused finding is F10, where F5's new stagedEntryKind ignored short reads despite the agent calling it a total classifier.
guidance_observations: Pushbacks in this PR carried checkable evidence (ls-remote, git ls-files -s, a scratch pnpm 10 install, quoted pnpm constants), which is the model for refuting reviewer guesses.
The round-0 README fixes corrected the flagged lines only; a full reread of the rewritten README sections against code would have removed F7 and F11 a round earlier.

evidence: The PR widened transposedResolver's key to four ThemeKey axes and fixed the cache key, but the unit suite's only helper was hueKey, which sets every axis but hue to identity. 2381da5 added chromaScale, lightnessScale -1, and memo-collision tests, all measured in OKLCH.
guidance_note: When a function's key grows new axes (and its cache key is changed to cover them), add one unit test per new axis plus a cache-collision test at that layer in the same PR.

evidence: effectiveLookName took Record<string, unknown> although its result always feeds lookKeyByName, which expects Record<string, ThemeKey>, and ThemeKey was already imported in policy.ts. The agent checked every caller already passed ThemeKey maps, so tightening the type was free.
guidance_note: When a parameter is deliberately loosened, check whether the type it really needs is already imported; if it is, use the precise type.

narrative: This was a clean feature PR. Round 0 raised two advisory findings, a missing unit test for the new ThemeKey axes and a loose parameter type; both were valid and fixed in one commit (2381da5). Round 1 found nothing, and no finding was caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: Both findings were cheap to accept and the agent checked callers before tightening the type; nothing in this PR's process cost an extra round.

evidence: pidAlive's EPERM-returns-true branch had no test; only the own-pid and exited-pid cases were covered. 2d877ee added pidAlive(1). That test exercises EPERM only for a non-root runner, though it passes either way.
guidance_note: Every explicit error-code branch in a new function gets its own test in the PR that adds it.

evidence: The new killTree rethrew non-ESRCH errors where the cleanup it replaced had wrapped child.kill in a try/catch, so a throw would skip release() and the rmSync calls. The trigger the reviewer named (EPERM on the suite's own process group) is far-fetched. The agent took the reviewer's second option and made killTree never throw.
guidance_note: When replacing a guarded best-effort call with a helper, carry the guard's error contract into the helper.

evidence: This has the same root cause as F2, in the afterEach loop, and the same source-level killTree change in 2d877ee closes it.
guidance_note: When replacing a guarded best-effort call with a helper, carry the guard's error contract into the helper.

evidence: makeFixture created three mkdtempSync dirs with a 'cc-candybar-poolit-' prefix. The finally block only killed and released, and global-teardown sweeps only 'cc-candybar-jest-*'. 2d877ee added a fixture cleanup().
guidance_note: When a fixture creates temp dirs, have it return their cleanup and call it from finally in the same test; then grep the PR for other fixtures that create dirs.

evidence: The leak path is real: d1 and d2 were spawned before the try block, so a d2 throw skipped d1's cleanup. But 'runs indefinitely' is wrong, because test/setup.ts anchors every worker via CC_CANDYBAR_PARENT_PID and the fixture env spreads process.env. 2d877ee nested a try/finally after each spawn, but left the pending d3Promise uncovered (F13).
guidance_note: When restructuring cleanup for spawned processes, enumerate every handle, including promises still pending, and trace each throw point to its cleanup.

evidence: The tryClaim comment claimed read-back 'correctly reports failure', but a read-back that lands before the other racer's rename lets both succeed. The reviewer only asked for the overclaim to be noted, and 2d877ee rewrote the comment. However, the release() and sweepStale() docs carried the same overclaim and were left untouched (F10, F12).
guidance_note: When correcting one overstated concurrency guarantee, grep the module for every other doc that claims safety under concurrency and correct them in the same commit.

evidence: SlotRecord and LeaseRecord independently declared {pid, startTime}, and 2d877ee extracted ProcessIdentity into process-fingerprint.ts. It unified the type only; the parse/validation of that identity stayed duplicated and diverged (F19).
guidance_note: When extracting a shared identity type, also extract or align the parser and validator that produce it.

evidence: The sweep is one readdirSync per full test run plus an in-memory prefix filter, which costs microseconds. The proposed hand-maintained cleanup list adds a second registry that drifts when a caller forgets to register. The agent recorded the rationale in a code comment in 4b6ce10.

global-teardown's isConnectable used a connect probe as its liveness test. That is the false-dead signal socket-lease.ts was introduced to replace (ECONNREFUSED on a full backlog). 4b6ce10 switched it to readLease plus sameLiveProcess.
guidance_note: When writing a new liveness check, use the codebase's existing liveness authority (lease plus fingerprint) instead of re-deriving it with a probe that authority was built to replace.

evidence: release()'s doc 'Removes the slot file only if it still names us' overclaims in the same way as the tryClaim comment F6 fixed. The check-then-unlink is a TOCTOU, and 2d877ee corrected only tryClaim's comment. The reviewer offered a lock; the agent corrected the doc, which is consistent with F6's accepted test-tooling tradeoff.
guidance_note: When correcting one overstated concurrency guarantee, grep the module for every other doc that claims safety under concurrency and correct them in the same commit.

evidence: The agent ran a throwaway test confirming that process.env.CC_CANDYBAR_PARENT_PID equals the worker pid inside Jest (set by test/setup.ts). Fixtures spread process.env, so the daemons are anchored and the watchdog kills them when the worker dies. This repeats the overstatement already corrected on F5.

sweepStale's doc claimed it was 'safe to call even while another concurrent worktree's suite is mid-run', despite the race between its check and its unlink. This is the same overclaim class F6's comment fix left unswept. 4b6ce10 corrected the doc rather than adding a re-read.
guidance_note: When correcting one overstated concurrency guarantee, grep the module for every other doc that claims safety under concurrency and correct them in the same commit.

evidence: F5's restructure (2d877ee) wrapped d1 and d2 in their own try/finally and claimed 'a later spawn throwing can never leak an earlier one'. But if an assertion threw, d2's release unblocked the un-awaited d3Promise, which then spawned a daemon with no handle. The 'no watchdog' part is wrong because setup.ts anchors workers. f6768e1 drained d3Promise in cleanup.
guidance_note: When restructuring cleanup for spawned processes, enumerate every handle, including promises still pending, and trace each throw point to its cleanup.

evidence: Planting {pid: deadPid, startTime: null} makes sameLiveProcess fall back to pidAlive, so a recycled pid would read as live. Recording the real start time before killing the process exercises the fingerprint path the pool exists to use. This was narrow, but the fix was cheap and more faithful.
guidance_note: Test fixtures for identity checks should use the full identity the production path compares, not a degraded null fallback.

evidence: The reviewer itself notes that 'The comment lines 106-119 acknowledge this' and asks only for the decision to be recorded. The race is real but was already documented and accepted under F6.

The reviewer assumes setup.ts creates the dir with mkdtempSync; the agent says it only builds a path string with randomUUID. setup.ts is not in the packet, but the teardown comment calls the path 'dormant today', consistent with the agent. The reviewer itself offered 'accept the risk if the dormant path stays dormant', so declining was right either way.
A mkdirSync with recursive:true ran inside tryClaim on every poll of every slot. It was a no-op after the first call, so hoisting it into createDaemonPool was a correct trivial cleanup.
guidance_note: Hoist setup a function only needs once out of its retry loop.

evidence: spawnDaemon in daemon-shutdown.test.ts created three tmpdirs before 'await spawnTestDaemon(env)' and built its cleanup only afterwards. This is the same tmpdirs-before-spawn leak F4 fixed only in daemon-pool.test.ts's makeFixture. ab374eb wrapped the spawn in a cleanup-on-failure.
guidance_note: When fixing a temp-dir leak in one test fixture, grep for every fixture that creates dirs and then spawns, and fix them all in the same commit.

evidence: readSlot accepted any number as a pid, including 0, where process.kill(0, 0) signals the caller's own group, while readLease requires Number.isInteger and pid > 0. F7's fix unified the ProcessIdentity type but left the two parsers diverged. ab374eb mirrored readLease's validation.
guidance_note: When extracting a shared identity type, also extract or align the parser and validator that produce it.

evidence: spawn() reports ENOENT through an async 'error' event. With no listener, Node throws it as unhandled, crashing the worker, and the exit-driven slot release never fires. ab374eb added child.once('error', releaseOnce).
guidance_note: Every spawned ChildProcess gets an 'error' listener next to its 'exit' listener.

evidence: acquire checked its deadline only after a full scan, and each scan could spawn ps with a 2000ms timeout, so timeoutMs was a floor rather than a ceiling. The reviewer concedes ps normally takes under 50ms. fe0906e checks the deadline after every tryClaim.
guidance_note: When a loop body can block, check the deadline per blocking call, not per outer iteration.

narrative: This PR adds a machine-global daemon pool for tests and ran five review rounds. Five later findings trace to round-0 fixes that handled only the flagged instance. F6's comment correction missed the identical overclaims in release() and sweepStale() (F10, F12). F5's spawn-cleanup restructure missed the pending d3Promise (F13). F4's tmpdir-leak fix missed daemon-shutdown's spawnDaemon (F18). F7's shared ProcessIdentity type left the parsers diverged (F19). Every round also carried original-code findings, so no whole round was avoidable, but each of rounds 1–3 contained fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: The dominant cost here was fixing the cited line instead of the class: each round-0 fix needed a grep across the PR's other test files and docs for the same shape.

The reviewer twice repeated the 'un-anchored daemon' claim after the agent corrected it on F5; the agent's empirical check on F11 settled it, but adding a one-line comment at makeFixture noting the inherited anchor would have pre-empted the repeat.
